items.title: Joe Wilder Part 1 interviewed by Monk Rowe, Sarasota, Florida, April 12, 1996
items.q: I joined Lionel Hampton’s band from Les Hite’s band. And I was in Lionel Hampton’s band in 1943... when I came out I went back with Lionel Hampton

ctx.x: Did you get to do some traveling at that point, around the country, did you travel?

Yes, we traveled quite a bit, right. And from that band, I finally went, I joined Lionel Hampton’s band from Les Hite’s band. And I was in Lionel Hampton’s band in 1943 at the time I went into the service.
Can you give — we have a student sitting watching this tape — can you give him an idea of what it was like to be in a large group, and crisscrossing the country at that time?

items.title: Joe Wilder — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: I was not with them a full year, because I left them and went with Lionel Hampton.

ctx.x: Did you feel you learned a lot? How long were you with the band? About a year?
I was not with them a full year, because I left them and went with Lionel Hampton.

items.title: Joe Wilder Part 2 interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, October 12, 1998
items.q: I joined that band and I was making eleven dollars a night, and I was playing, at that time, the first trumpet part.

ctx.x: It wasn’t the easiest gig in the world, from what I understand.

It wasn’t, no it wasn’t. There were many times when it wasn’t. And the funny thing of it is that my antagonism towards Lionel didn’t come from anything he did to me personally, it was things that they did to other people that you were witness to you know. For instance the bass player, Vernon Alley, a very fine bass player, he became ill. We were someplace in Texas. And the doctor said he had the flu or something and he has to stay in bed for at least a week. And so it was like okay, they gave him the money that…
Were you aspiring to play in a classical situation at that time also?
